title: Expires must be at least params.minDaysRemaining days in the future

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: Security.txt implementations are RECOMMENDED to use an Expires date of no more than a year in the future. RFC 9116 places no lower bound on how far out Expires must be, and does not require a warning window before expiry.
spec.note: conformance_testable is false because RFC 9116 imposes no minimum-days-remaining threshold -- see policy_note. §2.5.5 was fetched from the immutable rfc9116.txt on 2026-07-30 (ADR 0011 follow-up (a)); the normative_quote here paraphrases the RECOMMENDED "less than a year" sentence and mixes in local commentary, so verified_against_source is false (see verification_note). The 30-day floor is a local operational buffer, not an RFC requirement.
spec.verification_note: clause §2.5.5 is cited, but normative_quote PARAPHRASES the RFC's RECOMMENDED "less than a year" sentence and appends local commentary rather than transcribing §2.5.5 verbatim (confirmed against the immutable rfc9116.txt on 2026-07-30). The operative 30-day floor is a local threshold (params.minDaysRemaining), not an RFC requirement, so this rule is local-policy and the conformance gate does not require verification; it is not marked verified because the quote is not a faithful source transcription.

policy_note: RFC 9116 §2.5.5 requires only that Expires be future-dated (see security-txt-expired) and RECOMMENDS under one year (OQ5, deferred to the first ratchet increment). The 30-day floor here is a LOCAL operational buffer so the monthly audit cadence (audit-web.yml monthly job) gets at least one warning cycle before the file actually expires. It is supplied by params.minDaysRemaining and read by check-security-txt.mjs on the production path (main()'s call to validateSecurityTxt) -- it is not restated as a separate literal in the validator.
applicability: A security.txt body containing a parseable, non-past Expires value.
expectation: The parsed Expires instant is at least params.minDaysRemaining days after the evaluation instant.

cases.name: exactly at the threshold passes -- the comparison is strict (<), not (<=)
40 days out -- probe C perturbs params.minDaysRemaining past this to prove it is the real comparison operand
no Expires field -- this rule is inapplicable, security-txt-expires-missing fires instead
